sources: Volcano: discovered in 1848 by Colonel Stevenson's men, who mined Soldiers Gulch in 1849; hydraulic operations began in 1855 (California OHP, Historical Landmark No. 29, plaque text): https://ohp.parks.ca.gov/ListedResources/Detail/29

Name: the camp was called Soldiers Gulch; miners renamed it Volcano in 1850 'because of the volcanic appearance of the location' (NRHP nomination, St. George Hotel, 1984, section 8). Secondary source, not independently verified: https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/GetAsset/NRHP/84000757_text

St. George Hotel: its predecessor burned in 1862; the NRHP nomination dates the present brick hotel to 1867, while other accounts (e.g. HMDB marker 11785, not read directly) give 1863-64. Both are after 1849: https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/GetAsset/NRHP/84000757_text
Cobblestone Theatre: built 1856 as Adolph Mayer's Tobacco and Cigar Emporium; leased by the Volcano Theatre Company from 1974 (Volcano Theatre Company, About): https://volcanotheatre.net/about/

Observatory: George Madeira's observatory, first amateur astronomical observatory of record in California, where he found the Great Comet of 1861 (California OHP, Landmark No. 715). The 1860 build year is from secondary accounts: https://ohp.parks.ca.gov/ListedResources/Detail/715
Old Abe: Civil War episode, 1860s (California OHP, Landmark No. 29): https://ohp.parks.ca.gov/ListedResources/Detail/29
UNVERIFIED, retained as a lead: 'oak and grass three to five feet high (Cook, 1849)' has no retrievable citation in this repo.

later_sites.label: St. George Hotel
later_sites.notYet: Washed ground and mist. The brick hotel is 1860s: 1863 or 1867, the records disagree.

later_sites.label: Cobblestone Theatre
later_sites.notYet: No stone building yet. It goes up in 1856 as a cigar shop; the theatre company comes in 1974.

later_sites.label: Observatory site
later_sites.notYet: Bare rise. Madeira's telescope comes about 1860; his comet is 1861.

later_sites.label: Old Abe cannon
later_sites.notYet: No gun on this corner in 1849. Old Abe is a Civil War errand.
